title: Parse CSV, quotes and all
why: Delimiters inside quotes, an escaped quote, a newline inside a field, CRLF, and the two boundary cases (empty input, trailing newline) are where a naive `split(',')` fails. This is the cheapest task here and it is still one a split()-based answer gets wrong.
requirements: Write `src.js` exporting `parseCsv(text)` that returns an array of rows, each row an array of string fields. A field wrapped in double quotes may contain commas and newlines. Two double quotes inside a quoted field mean one literal quote. Accept both \n and \r\n as a row separator. Empty input is an empty array, and a trailing newline does not produce a trailing empty row. Do not add dependencies.
